summary: The ICTP Postgraduate Diploma Programme is a one-year, pre-PhD course at the Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics in Trieste, Italy, running from 1 September to 31 August. It has been offered since 1991 to young graduates from UN, UNESCO or IAEA member countries in one of five physics and mathematics fields. Tuition is free, and ICTP offers a limited number of scholarships with a travel grant to candidates from developing countries, with priority for the least developed regions. Students finish with a dissertation they submit and defend.
eligibility_notes:
Who: young, qualified graduates in physics, mathematics or a related field, who are citizens of UN, UNESCO or IAEA member countries. Applicants are generally below 28 years of age (the page also says 'under the age of 28').

Degree: a degree equivalent to an MSc, or an exceptionally good BSc. An MSc is preferred in the summary box. The FAQ explains that 'exceptionally good' means at least a first-class honours degree together with your referees' confirmation that you performed exceptionally well. A BSc holder is eligible to apply, and you can apply if your BSc is in another subject (such as engineering, biology or chemistry) and the selection committee decides.

Language: the programme is in English, and fluency in speaking and writing is essential. TOEFL or IELTS is not mandatory and no GRE or TOEFL minimum is set; instead you give proof of English in the online application, such as an approved test result, a document showing your degree was taught in English, or a self-declaration for native speakers.

Expected background by field: Condensed Matter and Statistical Physics: solid state physics, quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, classical mechanics, electrodynamics and mathematical physics. High Energy, Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics: classical mechanics, electrodynamics, special relativity, quantum mechanics and statistical mechanics. Earth System Physics: a theoretical background in physics, mathematics or engineering plus mathematical methods used in geophysics and geosciences. Mathematics: basic abstract algebra, elements of real and complex analysis, and topology. Quantitative Life Sciences: classical mechanics, thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, mathematical methods for physics, and basic programming.

You can apply to one field only. Candidates without a scholarship may attend at their own cost if they meet the same selection criteria and give written proof of funding (see benefits).
age_experience_notes: Applicants are 'generally below 28 years of age'; this is a general guide rather than a stated hard limit. No work-experience requirement is stated.
funding_summary: There are no tuition fees. ICTP awards a limited number of scholarships, around 10 per field, to candidates from developing countries, with priority for the least developed regions; they cover travel and living expenses for the full year at the Centre, with a travel grant for scholarship holders. The scholarship amount is not stated. A limited number of qualified candidates may attend at their own cost with written evidence from a funding agency or bank that funds for the whole year are available and equal to those the Centre offers. ICTP gives no support for spouses or family members.
programmes_note: Five fields (choose one): High Energy, Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics; Condensed Matter and Statistical Physics; Earth System Physics; Mathematics; Quantitative Life Sciences. The programme has two semesters of classes (courses by term, listed under the level), then a research project and a dissertation that must be submitted and defended. Each field has a coordinator. The page also lists Science, Technology and Innovation as a field but names no diploma courses for it.
institutions_note: ICTP, Strada Costiera 11, Trieste, Italy. ICTP is governed by the IAEA, Italy and UNESCO and is a UNESCO Category 1 Institute. Students do all coursework at the Centre.

summary.detail: One-year postgraduate diploma course in English, 1 September to 31 August, followed by a dissertation. Entry: a degree equivalent to an MSc, or an exceptionally good BSc, with the background listed for the chosen field. Courses run in terms: for example in Mathematics Term I (7 September to 7 November 2026) has Real Analysis, Topology and Algebra, all mandatory, and Term II (23 November 2026 to 12 February 2027) has Functional Analysis and Complex Analysis plus a choice of Differential Geometry or Supervised Machine Learning. In High Energy, Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics the Term I courses include Quantum Mechanics, Lorentz Invariant Classical Field Theory, General Relativity I and Quantum Field Theory I. Condensed Matter courses include Statistical Mechanics, Electrons and Phonons in Solids, Advanced Quantum Mechanics and Scientific Python. Earth System Physics courses include Wave Physics, Climate Physics, Geophysical Fluid Dynamics and, in Term II, a climate track and a solid-earth track. Quantitative Life Sciences courses include Probability, Stochastic Processes, Ecology and Evolution, Supervised Machine Learning and a Spring College on the Physics of Complex Systems.

programmes.name: High Energy, Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics
programmes.detail: Coordinator G. Villadoro. Term I (Sep 2026 to Jan 2027): Quantum Mechanics; Lorentz Invariant Classical Field Theory; General Relativity I; Quantum Field Theory I. Term II (Jan to May 2027): Standard Model I; Quantum Field Theory II; Standard Model II; General Relativity II.
programmes.source_text: High Energy, Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics (Coordinator: G. Villadoro)

programmes.name: Condensed Matter and Statistical Physics
programmes.detail: Coordinator Nicola Seriani. Term I (Sep to Dec 2026): Mathematical Techniques; Linux Basics; Numerical Methods I; Statistical Mechanics; Electrons and Phonons in Solids; Advanced Quantum Mechanics; Selected Topics in CMP. Term II (Jan to Apr 2027): Scientific Python; Numerical Methods II; Superconductivity and Magnetism; Electronic Structure; Advanced Statistical Mechanics.

programmes.name: Earth System Physics
programmes.detail: Coordinator Riccardo Farneti. Term I (Sep to Dec 2026): Wave Physics; Physics of the Earth for Geohazards; Atmospheric Thermodynamics; Climate Physics; Geophysical Fluid Dynamics; Linux Basics; Numerical Methods I; Scientific Python. Term II (Jan to May 2027): Numerical Methods and Data Analysis in GeoScience for all, then a Climate track (Atmospheric Dynamics, Ocean Dynamics, BioGeochemical Cycles, Earth System Modelling) or a Solid Earth track (Theoretical Seismology, Space Geodesy and InSAR, Applied Seismology, Physics of Volcanoes, Mechanics of Earthquakes and Tectonophysics, Observations and Computer Methods).

programmes.name: Mathematics
programmes.detail: Coordinator Pavel Putrov. Term I (7 Sep to 7 Nov 2026), all mandatory: Real Analysis; Topology; Algebra. Term II (23 Nov 2026 to 12 Feb 2027): Functional Analysis and Complex Analysis (mandatory) plus one of Differential Geometry or Supervised Machine Learning. Term III (1 Mar to 30 Apr 2027): Algebraic Topology (mandatory) plus two of ODE and Dynamical Systems, Algebraic Geometry, Partial Differential Equations, Representation Theory.

programmes.name: Quantitative Life Sciences
programmes.detail: Coordinator Matteo Marsili. Term I (Sep 2026 to Feb 2027): Probability; Large Scale Behaviour; Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics; Stochastic Processes; Ecology and Evolution; Scientific Python; Mathematical Methods. Term II (Feb to Jun 2027): Spring College on the Physics of Complex Systems; Supervised Machine Learning; Reinforcement Learning; Introduction to Neuroscience; Introduction to Mathematical Economics; Statistical Learning.

requirements.text: Online application form, submitted in the ICTP online application system.

Transcripts and degree certificates, in English, uploaded with the application. If you have not yet finished your BSc and have no official transcript, you give your current status in the online application.
Documents showing that you can follow advanced courses and write scientific English.
Proof of English: an approved language test result, a document showing your degree was taught in English, or a self-declaration for native speakers. TOEFL, IELTS and GRE are not mandatory.
requirements.conditional_rule: also required if your courses were taught in English

requirements.text: Two letters of recommendation from senior scientists who know your work. Referees send them through the online application system (by invitation from the system), not by email.
Originals or certified copies of transcripts and degrees, with certified English translations, to be provided before admission.
Written proof of funding for the whole year from a funding agency or bank, equal to the Centre's offer.
requirements.conditional_rule: only if you want to attend at your own cost

application_steps.title: Choose one field and check your background
application_steps.detail: Pick one of the five fields (you cannot apply to two) and check the background expected for it. You can still apply if your degree is in a neighbouring subject; the selection committee decides.

application_steps.title: Complete the online application and upload documents
application_steps.detail: Fill in the online application form and upload transcripts and degree certificates in English, documents showing your ability to follow advanced courses and write scientific English, and proof of English. Invite two senior scientists to send recommendation letters through the online system. You can edit your application until the deadline, and documents cannot be added afterwards. The 2026-2027 call gave 15 March 2026 as its deadline after an extension; the programme page now shows 28 February 2027.

application_steps.title: Committee selection
application_steps.detail: The selection committee chooses the most academically qualified candidates on the basis of university record and academic recommendations, while aiming for gender balance and geographic distribution. Scholarships go first to candidates from developing countries, especially the least developed regions.

application_steps.title: Decision by May
application_steps.detail: According to the FAQ, you are usually notified by May of the year the course begins, if not earlier.

application_steps.title: Send certified documents before admission
application_steps.detail: If selected, provide originals or certified copies of transcripts and degrees, with certified English translations, before you are admitted.

application_steps.title: Study at ICTP for one year
application_steps.detail: The year runs from 1 September to 31 August with two semesters of classes in terms by field, then a research project. Students are examined on the courses.

application_steps.title: Write and defend the dissertation
application_steps.detail: After the courses and examinations, each participant writes a dissertation, which must be submitted and defended. Graduates have gone on to PhDs in Europe and North America.
